pathfinder.caption: The 'Presidential Panorama' from the Mars Pathfinder lander in Ares Vallis, with the Sojourner rover pasted in at several spots it visited.
pathfinder.note: The same rover appears several times: rover frames from different days were composited into one scene. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (62 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

sojourner.caption: The 'Presidential Panorama' from the Mars Pathfinder lander in Ares Vallis, with the Sojourner rover pasted in at several spots it visited.
sojourner.note: The same rover appears several times: rover frames from different days were composited into one scene. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (62 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

viking1.caption: Viking 1's camera 1 survey panorama of Chryse Planitia, its second picture from Mars (PIA00391).
viking1.note: Black-and-white. hfov from the survey-mode scale of 0.12 deg/px (2501 px is about 300 deg); 512 lines is about 61 deg. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (61 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

viking2.caption: Viking 2 lander survey panorama of Utopia Planitia.
viking2.note: Black-and-white. hfov is estimated from the survey-mode scale of 0.12 deg/px. A colorized 1976 version exists (File:Panorama-VikingLander2-1-1976.jpg) but covers less of the horizon. The Commons page gives no exact date. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (62 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

spirit.caption: 'Calypso' Pancam panorama from 'Troy', the spot beside Home Plate in Gusev Crater where Spirit got stuck and later fell silent.
spirit.note: The caption says north is at the center and south at both ends, so the left edge faces 180 deg. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (79 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

opportunity.caption: Opportunity's last panorama (the 'Legacy Pan', PIA22908), 354 Pancam images taken in Perseverance Valley just before the 2018 dust storm silenced the rover.
opportunity.note: Downscaled from the unlabeled PIA22908_full.tif; the Commons copy has text labels. False color, as released. Some frames at lower left are black-and-white because the pan was never finished. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (80 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

phoenix.caption: Full-circle approximately true-color panorama of the Phoenix landing site on the arctic plains of Mars, showing polygon-patterned ground, the deck and both solar arrays.
phoenix.note: Cylindrical projection. The caption says the image center faces west, so the left edge is assumed to face 90 deg (east). vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (85 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

insight.caption: InSight's sol 14 panorama of 'Homestead Hollow' in Elysium Planitia, taken with the arm-mounted Instrument Deployment Camera (PIA23140).
insight.note: The caption states a 290 deg view. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (27 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

curiosity.caption: Curiosity's 360-degree Mastcam view of a field of polygons on Mount Sharp, sols 4930-4931 (PIA26729).
curiosity.note: Newest Curiosity 360 found (released 2026-07-29). The rover is still driving, so this is a recent stop. The horizon is tilted because the rover sits on a slope; the black areas are uncovered sky and ground. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (99 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

perseverance.caption: Perseverance's 980-image Mastcam-Z 360-degree panorama of 'Crocodile Bridge' on Jezero Crater's rim (PIA26699).
perseverance.note: Newest color Perseverance 360 found. A Feb 2026 Navcam 360 at Mala Mala (PIA26704) exists but is black-and-white. The rover is still driving. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (82 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

ingenuity.caption: Perseverance's 67-image Mastcam-Z mosaic of 'Valinor Hills'. Ingenuity is the tiny speck just left of center, where its 72nd and final flight ended.
ingenuity.note: Partial view taken from about 415 m away, not from the helicopter. hfov of about 180 deg is a rough guess (not stated). The helicopter is only a few pixels at this size. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (41 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

apollo11-lm.caption: Neil Armstrong's Panorama 4 at Tranquility Base (AS11-40-5930 to 5941), with the Lunar Module Eagle and Buzz Aldrin.
apollo11-lm.credit: NASA/Neil Armstrong; panorama assembly Yuri Krasilnikov
apollo11-lm.note: Commons marks the volunteer-stitched panorama public domain. The black sky is real. hfov 360 is assumed. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (105 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.

surveyor3.caption: Apollo 12 view across Surveyor Crater, home of Surveyor 3, with the Intrepid LM on the rim (AS12-46-6746/6748/6763).
surveyor3.note: Partial: about 3 Hasselblad frames (about 50 deg each), so hfov of about 137 deg is an estimate. Surveyor 3 itself is not prominent in this view. vtop/vbottom are estimates: vfov is about hfov*h/w (50 deg), split at the visually estimated horizon.
